catalog_quote: (a) Elfenbein 1984 [scanned, 'd' = schwa]: The following notes are intended as a commentary on the account of the language given in LZ. PHONOLOGY (Cf. LZ, p. 567) (i) A stressed short a is often lengthened, and an unstressed long a shortened, ... (vi) The standard weakening of final vowels in Wan makes the m/f gender distinction much less audible: d and a are not phonemically distinct when unstressed in any position. But stressed final -d is kept apart from stressed -a, as in PS. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check passes: every segment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held files at the stated places (Elfenbein 1984 pp. 56-57 by scanned running heads; Wikipedia Stress section; EIr). (2) But the deciding evidence is weak in kind and custody: the word-level contrast and the aspectual verb-stress shift that make the LEXICAL call come from an uncited Wikipedia section, and the primary leg is three scanned pages of a 1984 journal sketch scraped from a shadow-library preview. Before this audit none of Glottolog's four descriptive works was held. (3) I fetched sources the fullest sketch, Elfenbein 1967 (ArOr 35, open via the Czech Academy Kramerius), and read pp. 563-607: p. 578 states a 'strong stress-accent' with reduction of all unaccented vowels to ə, p. 568(a) lists words 'accented differently in Wan and Pš', accent marks in the texts fall on varying syllables, and no positional or weight

sources.citation: Elfenbein, Josef. 1967. 'Laṇḍa, zor wəla! Waṇecī'. Archiv Orientální 35: 563-606 [scanned text of pp. 563-607 plus page images of pp. 563, 567, 568, 578, 579; Czech Academy of Sciences Library Kramerius, licence knav_public_contract].
sources.quote: p. 578 (page image read): 'A characteristic of the language is a strong stress-accent, noted by me often as a long vowel, and by G. Morgenstierne with an accent mark. All vowels can be reduced to ə when unaccented, and w and y are often reduced to ᵘ or ⁱ or dropped.' p. 568: 'a) Words accented differently in Wan and Pš: angīn 'honey' Pš gabīna; or- 'there' in compounds < ávaθra-, Pš war- < aváθra-; kubīr 'pigeon' Pš kautar; awlūn 'bridle' Pš mlūn'. No fixed-position or weight rule is stated anywhere in pp. 563-607; texts carry sporadic accent marks on varying syllables.
sources.locator: p. 578 (introduction to Texts); p. 568 note (a); p. 567 Phonology (refers phonology to NTS IV 158-162); p. 583 fn. 3 'The accent marks indicate stress.'
